papers.title_en: TurboWAM: Learning What Matters for Fast World Action Models
papers.authors: Guile Wu, Shuangzhi Li, Xingxin Chen, Chengjie Huang, Sam Hosseini, Tongtong Cao, Yingxue Zhang, Dongfeng Bai
papers.evidence: 面向机器人策略学习的快速世界动作模型
papers.tldr: 世界动作模型在机器人策略学习中表现突出，但推理延迟高，限制真实部署。TurboWAM 针对现有方法未区分视频世界模型各层对动作预测相关性的问题，提出结构化世界表示聚合，按动作去噪状态自适应融合多层表示。推理时减少执行层数并跨去噪步缓存相关表示，显著降低计算开销。在多个机器人操作基准上，它以较低延迟保持与先进方法有竞争力的成功率，为快速世界动作模型提供高效方案。
papers.abstract_en: World action models have demonstrated promising performance in robot policy learning, yet their high inference latency remains a critical bottleneck for real-world deployment. Recent approaches have sought to improve inference efficiency by reducing test-time future-frame imagination or accelerating action prediction. However, these methods often leverage representations from all video world model layers without explicitly considering their varying relevance to action prediction, leading to redundant computation and suboptimal representation utilization. In this work, we propose TurboWAM, a fast world action model that efficiently aggregates structured world representations conditioned on action predictions. Specifically, TurboWAM introduces a structured world representation aggregation module that adaptively fuses representations from different world model layers according to their relevance to the evolving action denoising state. Furthermore, TurboWAM employs a structured action supervision mechanism that adaptively modulates gradients from action supervision across different world model layers during backward propagation, facilitating world representation learning. During inference, by reducing the number of world model layers executed and caching relevant representations across action denoising steps, TurboWAM substantially reduces computational overhead. Extensive experiments on multiple robot manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that TurboWAM achieves low inference latency while maintaining competitive task success rates compared with state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title_en: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: static problems
papers.authors: Saugat Shahi, Filippo Fabiani, Mario Zanon
papers.tldr: 无信号交叉口自动驾驶车辆协调中，轨迹规划与通行顺序决策相互耦合，联合优化难以实际求解。本文提出分层启发式：下层用一系列非线性规划在给定顺序下优化各车轨迹，上层利用下层灵敏度信息设计新通行调度。多场景仿真表明，该方法较先进先出显著改善调度效果，同时保持计算可处理性。该工作为无信号交叉口耦合协调问题提供了兼顾调度质量与计算效率的求解思路。
papers.abstract_en: We consider the coordination of autonomous vehicles at unsignalized intersections, where trajectory planning and crossing-order decisions are intrinsically coupled, thereby making their simultaneous optimization intractable in practice. To this end, we propose a heuristic based on a hierarchical structure consisting of a series of nonlinear programs (NLP) in the lower level, which optimizes trajectories of each vehicle for a given crossing order, and a high-level heuristic to design new crossing schedules that exploits sensitivity information from the lower-level NLPs. Extensive numerical simulations across a broad range of traffic scenarios demonstrate that our strategy achieves substantially improved scheduling with respect to first-in-first-out ordering while preserving computational tractability.

papers.title_en: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: real-time algorithms
papers.authors: Saugat Shahi, Jonathan Frey, Filippo Fabiani, Moritz Diehl, Mario Zanon
papers.evidence: 多辆自动驾驶车辆的通行顺序与轨迹协同
papers.tldr: 无信号交叉口协调联网自动驾驶车辆时，通行顺序与车辆轨迹必须联合决策；固定顺序下问题可转化为双层优化，每辆车求解以进出时间为参数的最优控制问题，协调器再优化这些时间。本文利用实时软件acados的算法微分计算下层问题的一阶和二阶灵敏度，并采用定制算法高效求解上层协调问题。数值仿真验证了该实现具备实时可行性且协调效果有效。该工作为无信号交叉口实时最优协调提供了可部署的计算方案。
papers.abstract_en: When coordinating connected and automated vehicles at an unsignalized intersection, the crossing order and the vehicle trajectories must be decided jointly. For a fixed crossing order, the problem can be formulated conveniently in a bi-level form where each vehicle solves its own optimal control problem, whose optimal value is a function of its entry and exit times, and a coordinator optimizes these times subject to precedence constraints. We compute the first and second order sensitivities of lower-level problems, which are required to solve the upper-level problem, by means of algorithmic differentiation using the real-time software package \texttt{acados}. This implementation exploits tailored algorithms to obtain a computationally efficient implementation of the optimal coordination algorithm. We validate our implementation in numerical simulations that demonstrate both real-time feasibility and effectiveness of our algorithm.

papers.title_en: Open-World Object Motion Anticipation via Meta-Learned Semantic Adaptation
papers.authors: Mason Peterson, Gage MacLin, Camilla Tabasso, Jonathan P. How, Joshua Migdal, Tye Brady, Taskin Padir
papers.evidence: 面向仓储机器人安全导航的开放世界运动预判
papers.tldr: 机器人导航需预判周边物体运动，但新环境中未知物体及其交互关系难以在线适应。本文提出元学习图神经网络，融合语义、几何与关系历史，仅凭少量在线观测预测物体何时开始移动。方法仅在仿真训练，却能泛化到未见物体并无缝迁移硬件，优于视觉语言模型与类别频率基线。准确预判支撑闭环导航无碰撞通行，耗时与最快但易碰撞规划器相差四秒内。
papers.abstract_en: Anticipating the motion of nearby objects is critical for safe and efficient robot navigation. Without a proper understanding of what may move, a robot may plan overly conservative, inefficient trajectories to guarantee safety, or it may be overly risky, resulting in unacceptable collisions. While tracking and predicting the motion of known objects has seen significant progress, little research addresses how a robot should adapt online to novel objects, including anticipating how one object may move another (e.g., a person operating a forklift to move a pallet). To enable this capability, we propose a meta-learned graph neural network that leverages a semantic, geometric, and relational history of objects to accurately predict, from a few online observations, when objects will begin to move in new environments. We demonstrate that our method, which is trained only in simulation, accurately anticipates the motion of objects unseen at training time, transfers to hardware without any fine-tuning, and outperforms a vision-language model and a class-frequency baseline in both simulation and hardware experiments. Our method's accurate prediction enables collision-free traversals in a closed-loop navigation simulation, while remaining within four seconds of the fastest, collision-prone planner.
